title: How audiences heard Sauter-Finegan
summary: Dancers came, and Wild Wings in Iowa bewildered them.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You mentioned how people listen to music; how did people listen to Sauter-Finegan in 1954, say if you were on a typical one nighter?

Well, I think you have to realize that there were no groups around touring like that. The people who did come were mostly expecting to dance. It was sold as a dance band, which was unfortunate. We spent most of our time trying to satisfy them but never really doing it.
Did you pull out something like "Wild Wings of the Woods" once in a while?
Once in a while we did and I remember being in Iowa before that Lieberman concert in '54--we were at
practice or something--and towards the end of the evening we dragged that thing out and played our part and the people really didn't know what was going on. But some of them kind of liked it.
I'm sure that it must have been a totally different experience for most of them.
I think they were bewildered, a lot of them. Those who knew some of the records, did like it. They never did break down the gates to get in; that's for sure.
Which is the problem you had all along.
